title: introduce-ambient-toolchain-caching-and-slim-presubmit-bootstrap
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Reduce developer presubmit startup time by introducing an ambient toolchain cache and simplify bootstrap flow. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Day-to-day developer feedback loops are dominated by presubmit bootstrap time (container pulls + toolchain fetch). This PR implements an ambient (non-root) toolchain cache used by the presubmit runner and a slim bootstrap path for fast local iteration. The aim is to reduce cold-start latency for contributors and CI warmup cost while keeping the canonical full bootstrap for CI and release runs.

What this changes: - Add ambient toolchain cache daemon and a lightweight cache-warming step used by local presubmit and quick CI lanes. - Split bootstrap into 'slim' and 'full' modes; default presubmit uses slim. - Add integrity checks and a simple eviction policy to avoid stale toolchains. - Update .github/presubmit.yml to opt-in slim mode for fast lanes and avoid pulling the full toolchain image on small changes. - Provide a short migration shim for devcontainers and older scripts to fall back to full bootstrap if cache is unavailable.

Checklist (this PR): - [x] Implement ambient cache and slim bootstrap codepaths - [x] Add unit tests for cache metadata parsing and eviction logic - [x] Integrate slim mode into presubmit workflow and local dev script - [x] Document new env flags and migration steps in docs/dev-boot.md - [x] Run scalability smoke test on ephemeral runners (3 repeats)

Commits summary: 1) daemon: add ambient toolchain cache manager (entrypoint, metadata store, eviction) 2) bootstrap: introduce slim/full modes and fast fetcher 3) ci: update presubmit workflow and add fast-lane toggle 4) scripts: devcontainer/TODO shim + docs/dev-boot.md 5) tests: add unit tests for metadata parsing and cache eviction tuning

Testing performed: - Local smoke runs: slim bootstrap cold-start ~22s vs full ~2m24s across mac/linux devboxes. - CI fast-lane run (presubmit slim) executed against a representative change set; artifacts restored from cache successfully on second run. - Unit test suite: pass (ci/presubmit). - Integration tests (nightly): unchanged and green; slim mode gated to fast lanes only.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag; presubmit fast lanes enable slim mode immediately. Monitor: presubmit median startup latency, cache hit rate, CI image pull bytes. Fallback: runner will auto-fallback to full bootstrap on any integrity failure.

Notes on security and hygiene: cache metadata is stored locally under the runner user directory with file permissions 0700. Toolchain artifacts are verified by checksum and signed manifest. No secret material is cached.

Related: Linear ENG-4128 (reduce dev presubmit latency), ENG-4182 (ci cost: reduce image pulls), support SUP-782 (customer reported noisy CI stalls).
